clue.text: Nippers mentioned in part of the contract

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word for nippers is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a crab's nippers are its claws

explanation.surface: A contract has a section about pincers, or perhaps about small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' signals a sound-alike: CLAWS, said aloud, gives the contract term.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a single numbered section or provision within a legal agreement.

clue.text: Group in house beginning to roll into bed

indicators.note: these letters go into the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone at home starts to tumble into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: HO is a standard abbreviation for house, as in addresses; 'in' at the start is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a band or group of people, originally a Roman military unit.

clue.text: Small dish of tripe cooked with peas

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and changed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A starter of offal stewed with peas.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is a small course served before the main meal.

clue.text: Younger member of family — one of 5 forgetting name

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out a letter

parts.note: the answer to 5 down names four seasons, and spring is one of them

explanation.surface: A family's junior member forgets the name of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of 5' points to clue 5: Vivaldi's seasons. 'forgetting' drops N from SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig, literally a shoot, is used of a young person or offspring of a family.

clue.text: Repeated the thing time and time again to journalist

parts.note: it is the pronoun standing for a thing
an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: Someone told a reporter the same thing over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'time and time again' is split: one time is ERA, the second is T.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, so iterated is a direct synonym for repeated.

clue.text: Vivaldi's work an all-time favourite?

definitions.meaning: a set of violin concertos by the Italian composer
something liked all year round, whatever the weather

explanation.surface: Vivaldi's music is a perennial favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi's concertos are titled after spring, summer, autumn and winter, and something welcome in every one of them is liked all year.

clue.text: Given a new explanation by Oxford experts?

definitions.text: Given a new explanation by Oxford experts?

parts.words: Given a new explanation by Oxford experts?
parts.note: reads as a theory reinterpreted, but hints at dictionary editors at Oxford rewriting an entry's meaning

explanation.surface: Oxford scholars have reinterpreted something.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine is to give a new meaning or explanation, as a dictionary does to a word.

clue.text: A note that makes you feel good?

definitions.meaning: in music, the keynote of a scale

explanation.surface: A musical tone that cheers you up.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonic is the first note of a key, and is also a pick-me-up medicine.

clue.text: Remover of condensation could make me driest

indicators.note: the letters could make a new word once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget that clears fog could leave me dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A demister is a car device that blows air to clear misted windows.

clue.text: Work for the water board maybe, but be of no use?

definitions.text: Work for the water board maybe
definitions.meaning: literally, a job going down into the sewers

explanation.surface: Sewer work seems pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be wasted, and literally describes descending into a drain.

clue.text: Exaggerated claims could give Beryl hope

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could give a new word if they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big promises might lift the spirits of a woman called Beryl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could give' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of BERYL and HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is the figure of speech of deliberate overstatement, that is, exaggerated claims.

clue.text: Material taken from ground to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left

parts.note: ground that has been dug for ore or coal has been mined

explanation.surface: A fabric is being taken out of the earth somewhere westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' turns MINED round to give the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill cloth, the fabric of jeans.

clue.text: Rummage half-heartedly in rubbish

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle pair of letters, and only half of that pair survives

parts.note: to root around is to rummage

explanation.surface: Someone searches without enthusiasm through a heap of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle O's of ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is informal for nonsense or worthless stuff, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Helpful mediation to produce pleasant business accommodation

definitions.meaning: a phrase for help given as a go-between in a dispute
read literally, nice premises for a firm to work in

explanation.surface: Diplomatic help results in nice workspace.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names kindly intervention between parties, and literally reads as attractive commercial rooms.

clue.text: A bone outside black refuse container

indicators.note: the bone word sits outside the black letter, so it is cut open to hold it

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg, the shinbone
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bone lies beside a dark rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the opening 'A', which supplies the first letter. 'outside' puts SHIN round B.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash bin was originally for fireplace ashes and came to mean any dustbin for rubbish.

clue.text: Welsh chap beating a retreat in French street

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the street word

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Gene is a man's name, so a chap

explanation.surface: A man from Wales hurries backwards along a Paris road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' looks like a nationality but is the verb, to welsh on a bet; RENEGUE is an accepted variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to break a promise or fail to pay a debt, which is to renege; this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Executioner the reverse of tease nasty bit of work!

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
a rotter is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A hangman is anything but a joker: a really unpleasant man.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'tease' is just the word to be swapped for a synonym, then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotter kills by strangling with a cord or iron collar, an executioner's method.

clue.text: Try to get fish in beastly accommodation

parts.note: to have a stab is to try
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to catch fish in an awful lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' reads as horrible but means for beasts: horses' housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabling is housing for horses and other animals, accommodation for beasts.

clue.text: Mountain water is hard, giving stain

parts.note: a tarn is a small lake high in the hills
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Hard upland water leaves marks on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to discolour or sully, and as a noun it is a stain on a surface.

clue.text: Suffer death saintly being beheaded

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter

parts.note: a saintly person is pure

explanation.surface: A holy martyr suffers death by decapitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a martyred saint, but 'saintly' is the adjective giving the piece that loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or put up with hardship, so it means to suffer.

clue.text: Cliff-top walker may be nervous

definitions.meaning: literally at the brink of a drop

explanation.surface: Someone walking near a precipice may be anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tense or anxious, and literally a cliff walker is at the brink.

clue.text: Corrupted celebrity entertained by various baddies

indicators.note: a guest entertained by hosts is held inside them
various suggests the letters are taken in a different arrangement

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person falls into the company of assorted villains and is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupted' could be taken as an anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'various' is the one doing the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastardised means debased or made impure from its original form, so corrupted.

clue.text: Healthy place in holiday country

parts.note: a spa is a resort with healing mineral springs

explanation.surface: A health resort in a popular tourist land.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a European country hugely popular with British holidaymakers.

clue.text: Enjoy the food, girl —- and the booze!

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
gin is a spirit, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: An invitation to tuck in, with a young woman and drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an informal idiom for starting to eat heartily.

clue.text: Have dress shortened at the front

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, cut at the front

parts.note: a gown is a dress

explanation.surface: A tailor is asked to take a frock up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it.

clue.text: One part of army has a measure of intelligence about foreign national

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is the Royal Artillery, a branch of the British Army

indicators.note: about here means turned round

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: A soldier's IQ test concerns someone from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IQ to QI. 'has' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a citizen of Iraq, a national of a foreign country.

clue.text: Denied agent's involved in a plot

indicators.note: the jumbled piece goes in the plot word

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot of ground

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: agent is the word to scramble; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A spy is caught up in a conspiracy and turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'plot' is a conspiracy, but here it is a garden bed. 'involved' jumbles AGENT to NEGAT, which goes 'in' A BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or deny oneself something, so abnegated means denied.

clue.text: Pathological condition has horse turning unhealthy colour, we hear

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: we hear signals that the colour is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a sickly person is said to look green

explanation.surface: A horse is spinning round and looks green about the gills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses NAG to GAN; 'we hear' says the second part sounds like GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangrene is the death of body tissue from lost blood supply, a medical condition.

clue.text: False turn is disastrous and our wider community suffers a setback

indicators.note: something disastrous is in ruins, so the letters are scrambled
a setback sends things backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: for a British setter, the EU is the European Union, the wider community

explanation.surface: A political turn goes wrong and Europe takes a step back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disastrous' scrambles TURN to UNTR; 'suffers a setback' reverses EU to UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means not correct, a straightforward synonym of false.
